conflictOfInterest.details: The lesson author is VSBDev, who is also the operator of this review run. This is a declared founding-stage conflict of interest.

findings.finding: Scene 5 (content/05-clinical-wrap-up.md) actively teaches and applies core variables and controls concepts in a clinical context but is declared in lesson.json as having 'no-material-claims'. It lacks both claims mapping and a {source-note} block, which violates CONTENT-STANDARD.md Section 4.3 (stating that transfer scenes repeating sourced claims are not exempt).
findings.resolution: Update lesson.json to map scene-clinical-wrap-up to the relevant claims (claim-variable-roles, claim-confounder-ambiguity, claim-control-functions, claim-controls-have-limits), and add a corresponding {source-note} block at the end of content/05-clinical-wrap-up.md listing these claims and their respective sources.

findings.finding: The lessonVersion metadata property in assessment.json is declared as '0.1.1', which is inconsistent with the candidate lesson version of '0.2.0'.
findings.resolution: Change the value of lessonVersion in assessment.json to '0.2.0'.

findings.finding: The version in ATTRIBUTION.md is declared as '0.1.1', which is inconsistent with the candidate lesson version of '0.2.0'.
findings.resolution: Change the version string on line 6 of ATTRIBUTION.md to '0.2.0'.

findings.finding: The positive and negative control conditions are introduced purely as abstract, hypothetical concepts ('If the fictional comparison also supplied a positive-control condition...') in the clinical context, without providing a concrete medical example that a learner can easily picture.
findings.resolution: Provide a concrete medical example of controls, such as using a glucose meter manufacturer's control solution to verify meter responsiveness (positive control) or testing a zero-glucose solution/water (negative control) to check for background signal or calibration issues.

findings.finding: Although the lesson is reframed with a clinical context, none of the assessment items in assessment.json assess variables and controls in a clinical or medical scenario. They remain set in engineering, botany, physics, and laboratory detector contexts.
findings.resolution: Add or adapt at least one assessment item to evaluate variables, controls, and confounders in a clinical or medical setting, matching the new clinical focus of the lesson.

findings.finding: The first-read experience is highly engaging and effectively structured. The opening scenario of a reader showing '0' provides immediate concrete context, and the distinction between controlled variables and control conditions is explained clearly.
findings.resolution: No action required; maintain this clear and concrete introductory structure.

limitations: No real learners or independent human subject-matter experts tested this lesson draft.
The review was conducted solely on the source repository files using static analysis and validation scripts; no rendering or assistive technology paths were executed.
